key_insight: Halide substitution in Ca$_3$PX$_3$ strongly tunes the bandgap and photovoltaic performance, with Ca$_3$PI$_3$ emerging as the best solar-cell candidate.
engineering_relevance: The results provide a materials-selection guide for designing perovskite-inspired absorbers with higher efficiency and targeted optoelectronic properties.
method: SLME-based photovoltaic screening across X = F, Cl, Br, I
evidence_signal: All four compounds show direct bandgaps in the 2.0–3.788 eV range, and SLME identifies Ca$_3$PI$_3$ as highest at 29.6% while Ca$_3$PF$_3$ is lowest at 0.6%.
watch_item: The study is computational, so device-level efficiency may differ once synthesis, defects, and stability effects are considered.
paper_title: Halide substitution effects on the photovoltaic properties of Ca$_3$PX$_3$ (X = F, Cl, Br, I) perovskites: advancing solar cell efficiency
